# railway_bucket_cors_configuration (Resource)

Manages the ordered CORS configuration of a Railway bucket through its S3-compatible API.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "railway_bucket" "uploads" {
  name       = "uploads"
  project_id = railway_project.example.id
}

resource "railway_bucket_instance" "uploads" {
  bucket_id      = railway_bucket.uploads.id
  environment_id = railway_environment.example.id
  region         = "ams"
}

resource "railway_bucket_cors_configuration" "uploads" {
  project_id     = railway_project.example.id
  environment_id = railway_bucket_instance.uploads.environment_id
  bucket_id      = railway_bucket_instance.uploads.bucket_id

  cors_rules = [
    {
      id              = "browser-uploads"
      allowed_headers = ["*"]
      allowed_methods = ["GET", "HEAD", "PUT"]
      allowed_origins = ["https://example.com"]
      expose_headers  = ["ETag"]
      max_age_seconds = 3600
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bucket_id` (String) Identifier of the bucket.
- `cors_rules` (Attributes List) Ordered CORS rules. S3 applies the first rule matching an incoming request. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cors_rules))
- `environment_id` (String) Identifier of the environment where the bucket is deployed.
- `project_id` (String) Identifier of the project that owns the bucket.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of the bucket CORS configuration.

<a id="nestedatt--cors_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `cors_rules`

Required:

- `allowed_methods` (Set of String) HTTP methods allowed for matching origins.
- `allowed_origins` (Set of String) Origins allowed to access the bucket.

Optional:

- `allowed_headers` (Set of String) Request headers allowed in CORS preflight requests.
- `expose_headers` (Set of String) Response headers exposed to browser clients.
- `id` (String) Optional identifier for the CORS rule.
- `max_age_seconds` (Number) Duration in seconds that browsers may cache a preflight response.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import railway_bucket_cors_configuration.uploads project_id:environment_id:bucket_id
```
